prompt.context: Your client, SupplyCo., has three business lines: paper, janitorial supplies, and packaging supplies. Profitability is low at SupplyCo. The company has hired our firm to figure out why and to develop a solution for the problem.
prompt.question: Profitability is declining at SupplyCo. Why might this be, and what should the company do about it?

clarifying_info.q: How have sales volumes changed across business lines?
clarifying_info.a: Paper sales and packaging sales have declined; janitorial sales have remained steady.
Paper: large businesses and office supply stores. Janitorial supplies: large janitorial companies. Packaging: shipping companies and retailers with shipping service.
Preferences remain the same, but demand for paper is dropping with increased internet use.

clarifying_info.q: Are there new competitors or new entrants?

clarifying_info.a: Marketing has remained similar across the business lines.

clarifying_info.q: How does SupplyCo. distribute its products?
clarifying_info.a: Direct sales to large customers, internet sales for smaller customers, and distributors. This mix has not changed. Time to sale has remained constant.

clarifying_info.q: Are there substitutes affecting the business?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — email has replaced printing and mailing, reducing demand for both paper and packaging.

exhibits.title: Costs by Business Unit
exhibits.shows: A table comparing SupplyCo.'s cost ratios against competitor benchmarks (top 25% and bottom 25%) across three business units: Paper, Janitorial, and Packaging. Metrics shown include Revenue, COGS, SG&A, Inventory, COGS/Revenue, SG&A/Revenue, Net Income margin, and Inventory Turnover.

exhibits.title: Revenue Growth Options
exhibits.shows: Three strategic options (A, B, C) for revenue growth, each described with market size, average margin, competition, likely customer base, and expected market share.

Option_B_Recycled_Products.customers: Paper product companies, greeting card companies, suppliers to restaurants and coffee shops

Option_C_Janitorial_SMB.competition: Generally smaller supply companies; regional players

framework: Profitability: analyze revenue and costs by business line
Revenue: price trends, volume by segment, product mix shift
Costs: COGS (material, labor), SG&A (marketing, overhead), fixed vs. variable
Customers: who they are, preferences, demand drivers, B2B vs. B2C
Competitors: new entrants, differentiation, pricing, substitutes (internet/email)
Distribution: channels used (direct, internet, distributors), mix changes, time to sale

questions.prompt: Profitability is declining — what are some reasons that could be?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure around revenue and costs. Revenue levers: decreasing real prices (more discounts), reduced quantity (preference shifts, competitor influence), shift to less profitable product mix. Cost levers: increase in SG&A (e.g., increased marketing without sales lift), increased material costs, higher labor costs.

questions.prompt: How can we determine if our client's costs are too high? [Steer candidate to Exhibit 1.] After analysis: how could the client improve these ratios?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare SupplyCo.'s ratios to competitor benchmarks. Key finding: SupplyCo. is in the bottom 25% across all three business units on COGS/Revenue, SG&A/Revenue, Net Income, and Inventory Turnover. Improvement levers: (a) raise prices to improve revenue coverage of costs, (b) renegotiate supplier agreements to reduce COGS, (c) find cost efficiencies in back-office to reduce SG&A.

math.setup: Compare SupplyCo. implied ratios to top-25% competitor benchmarks. SupplyCo. total: Revenue $931M, COGS $829M, SG&A $88M. Implied COGS/Revenue = 829/931 = 89%. Implied SG&A/Revenue = 88/931 = 9.5%. Net income implied = (931-829-88)/931 = 14/931 = 1.5%.
steps: COGS/Revenue: 829/931 ≈ 89% — aligns with bottom-25% benchmark (88-91%) vs. top-25% of 77-83%
SG&A/Revenue: 88/931 ≈ 9.5% — aligns with bottom-25% benchmark (9-11%) vs. top-25% of 3-5%
Net Income: ~1.5% — aligns with bottom-25% (0-3%) vs. top-25% of 14-18%
Inventory Turnover: 331M inventory against 931M revenue implies ~2.8x — bottom-25% range (2.7-3.7) vs. top-25% of 4.3-5.1
math.answer: SupplyCo. is in the bottom 25% of competitors on every key cost metric across all three business units. Both COGS and SG&A ratios are far above top-quartile benchmarks, and net income margin is near zero.

questions.prompt: Brainstorm ideas for revenue growth. [After brainstorm, distribute Exhibit 2.] If the company needs to gain another $50 million in profit, which of the three options (A, B, C) should they pursue? They can pursue more than one.
questions.guidance: Brainstorm should cover: new customer segments (small/medium businesses for janitorial), new geographies, new product lines (recycled/green materials), pricing optimization, bundling, cross-selling across business lines. For the math, candidate should calculate profit for each option using market size × likely share × margin, then assess feasibility and strategic fit.

math.setup: Profit = Market Size × Likely Share × Margin for each option.
steps: Option A (Pharma): Likely share unknown — cannot calculate expected profit. Also completely outside core competency.
math.answer: Option A should not be pursued: expected share is unknown and the pharma market is completely outside SupplyCo.'s core competency. Options B and C together yield $40.5M + $10M = $50.5M in profit, narrowly exceeding the $50M target. Pursue B and C in tandem.

brainstorming.prompt: Brainstorm ideas for revenue growth at SupplyCo.

categories.name: New Customer Segments
ideas: Target small and medium businesses for janitorial supplies (currently only large companies)
Expand paper sales to educational institutions or government
Target e-commerce companies for packaging needs

categories.name: New / Adjacent Products
ideas: Launch recycled/green product lines (paper, cardboard, packaging)
Add complementary products (cleaning equipment alongside janitorial supplies)
Bundle paper and packaging for value-added offering

categories.name: Pricing and Mix
ideas: Shift product mix toward higher-margin items

categories.name: Channel and Sales
ideas: Increase direct sales force for mid-market customers
Develop partnerships with group purchasing organizations

categories.name: Customer Retention and Loyalty
ideas: Introduce long-term contracts with volume discounts
Improve customer service to reduce churn

recommendation: SupplyCo.'s costs are too high relative to its sales, placing it in the bottom quartile of competitors across all three business units.

The client should achieve greater operational synergies to reduce COGS and SG&A, and then pursue Options B (recycled products) and C (janitorial supplies for small/medium businesses) simultaneously to close the $50M profit gap.
risks: Reaching smaller companies for janitorial supplies may be more costly and could drive up SG&A costs
Entering the recycled products business will mean competing with established players
next_steps: Investigate costs associated with expanding the janitorial supplies sales network to small/medium businesses
Seek financing to support simultaneous expansion in two new markets
Begin supplier renegotiations and back-office efficiency review to improve cost ratios
